summary: Jakob Steiner studied at Heidelberg University (1818–1821) and the University of Berlin (1822–1824). He held posts at the University of Applied Sciences Berlin (1825–1834) and Frederick William University Berlin (1834–1863).

Jakob Wilhelm Hauer was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Basel Mission Seminary, Oxford, and Tübingen (PhD under Richard von Garbe, and Habilitation). He held posts at Marburg (1925–1927) and Tübingen (1927–1945).

James A. Benn works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge, SOAS, and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr., Timothy H. Barrett, and Jinhua Chen, and held posts at Lewis & Clark, McMaster, and Arizona State.

James A. Matisoff is a scholar of linguistics, Tibetology, and Sinology. He studied at Harvard, International Christian University, and UC Berkeley (PhD 1967). He taught at Columbia (1966–1969) and UC Berkeley (1970–2002).
James Adam was a scholar of philosophy. He completed his studies at the University of Aberdeen (~1876–1880) and Gonville and Caius College (~1880–1884).

James Atkinson worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies as well as Indology. After studying at the University of Edinburgh, he held posts at the India Government Mint in Kolkata and as Assistant Persian Professor at Fort William College in 1818.

James B. Apple is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed graduate studies and earned his PhD (1996) at the University of Wisconsin–Madison under doctoral supervisor John D. Dunne, alongside numerous other academic and traditional teachers.

James Blumenthal was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin–Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and studied at CIHTS. He held faculty posts at Oregon State University and Maitripa College.

James Burgess was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied at Glasgow and Edinburgh. He served as Secretary of the Bombay Geographical Society and held director roles and the Director General post at the Archaeological Survey of India (1886–1889).

James Burnell Robinson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Richard Hugh Robinson and Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and served as an associate professor of religious studies at the University of Northern Iowa (attested 1996).

James C. Dobbins is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his PhD from Yale University by 1984 and served as Fairchild Professor of Religion and East Asian Studies at Oberlin College (attested 2015–2019).

James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland was an Indology scholar. He studied at East India Company College and Fort William College under Thomas Roebuck, and later served as professor of law at Presidency University.

James Darmesteter was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Michel Bréal and Eugène-Louis Hauvette-Besnault, later holding posts at EPHE (~1877–1894) and Collège de France (1885–1894).

James Duerlinger is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin–Madison (~1964–1968) under Sheldon Pollock and became Professor Emeritus at the University of Iowa.
James Dwight Dana studied at Yale College (~1830–1833). He later held a post at Yale University from around 1850 to 1892.

James Fergusson was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who studied at the Royal High School, Edinburgh. He became a member of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland in 1840.
James Fieser is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Berea College and Purdue University (~1980–1986), and held a post at the University of Tennessee around 1992.
James G. Mullens is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at McMaster University and held a post at the University of Saskatchewan in 1989.

James H. Austin is a Buddhist studies scholar and neurologist. He studied under Nanrei Kobori and Katsujo Terayama, and held posts at the University of Oregon/OHSU (~1962–1967), University of Colorado (~1967–1992), and University of Florida.

James Hadley was a linguistics and Indology scholar. He studied at Fairfield Academy and Yale (under Edward Elbridge Salisbury in 1849). He tutored at Middlebury College (1845) and was professor of Greek at Yale University (1845–1872).
